metadata.title: The Hypervelocity Star SDSS J090745.0+024507 is a Short-Period Variable

evidence.quote: the Galactic halo star SDSS J090745.0+024507 (hereafter HVS)
In their survey of blue horizontal branch (BHB) stars, Brown et al. (2005) discovered that the Galactic halo star SDSS J090745.0+024507 (hereafter HVS)
well above the local escape speed from the Galaxy.
We present high-precision photometry of the hypervelocity star SDSS J090745.0+024507 (HVS)

notes: SDSS J090745.0+024507 is the sole eligible star. It is categorized as follow_up because T:p1-b7 states that Brown et al. (2005) discovered it as a Galactic halo star with a Galactic rest-frame radial velocity well above the local escape speed, while this paper presents follow-up photometry (T:p1-b4). 'HVS' is the paper's explicit abbreviation for this same star (T:p1-b7).

SDSS J090745.0+024507: RA and Dec are not tabulated separately; they are encoded in the SDSS J2000 designation printed in the paper. The paper reports a Galactic rest-frame radial velocity of 709 km/s (also ∼700 km/s) but no total three-dimensional Galactic-rest-frame speed or proper motions. Per the quantity definitions, that Galactic-rest-frame radial value is not recorded as radial_velocity (which excludes Galactic-rest-frame velocities) or as galactocentric_rest_frame_velocity (which requires a total three-dimensional speed). No parallax, proper motion, galactocentric radius, or bound/unbound probability is reported. Location T:p1-b8 contains the alternative distance values; T:p1-b4 gives the adopted 71 kpc heliocentric distance.
